summary:
## The ASC WordPress Plugin: An All-in-One Solution

The ASC plugin is a powerful, free tool designed to replace dozens of individual plugins, helping to clean up your dashboard, enhance security, and improve the performance of your WordPress site.

> [!TIP]
> The plugin organizes its many features into collapsible modules, allowing you to enable only the ones you need. You can find these settings under **Tools > Enhancements**.

## Admin Interface & Dashboard Cleanup

- **Hide Admin Notices**: Declutter your dashboard by hiding all non-essential admin notices, updates, and plugin messages with a single click.
- **Admin Menu Organizer**: Customize your WordPress admin menu by dragging and dropping items to reorder them, renaming menu titles, and hiding less-used items.

## Security Enhancements

- **Change Login URL**: Hide your site's login page by changing the URL from the default `/wp-admin` or `/wp-login` to a custom path.
  > [!IMPORTANT]
  > Once you set a new login URL, the old one will no longer work. Be sure to bookmark the new address!
- **Limit Login Attempts**: Protect against brute-force attacks by setting a maximum number of failed login attempts before a user's IP is temporarily blocked.

## Content & Code Management

- **Insert Custom Code**: Easily add custom scripts (like Google Analytics or tracking pixels) to your site's `<head>`, `<body>`, or footer without needing a separate plugin or editing theme files.
- **Content Duplication**: Duplicate any post or page with a single click, which is useful for creating new content based on an existing layout.
- **Custom Login Page Logo**: Replace the default WordPress logo on the login page with your own site's logo for consistent branding.

## Site Utilities & Performance

- **SMTP for Email Delivery**: Configure an SMTP service directly within the plugin to ensure that emails sent from your WordPress site (e.g., password resets, form notifications) are delivered reliably and don't end up in spam folders.
- **Maintenance Mode**: Activate a temporary maintenance page with a custom heading and message to inform visitors that your site is undergoing updates.
- **Redirect 404 to Homepage**: Automatically send visitors who land on a non-existent (404) page to your homepage, preventing user confusion.
- **Image Upload Control**: Improve site speed and save server space by setting maximum width and height dimensions. The plugin will automatically resize any images that exceed these limits upon upload.
transcription:
## The One Plugin to Rule Them All

What if you could replace 50 plus WordPress plugins with just one? Sounds crazy, right? But in this video, I'm going to show you the one powerful plugin that can clean up your dashboard, speed up your site, and keep it secure and simple, all without losing the features that you need. 

So, if your site feels bloated and slow, and you're tired of juggling too many plugins, this might be the plug-in that you'll ever need. So, watch the video till the end to learn how to use it. I'm Brian from Esite Learners, and let's get started.

## Disclaimer & Installing the ASC Plugin

This is not a sponsored video and we are not paid by ASC plug-in to make this video. We tried out several plugins and this one stood out because it has all the features we need in one place. 

So firstly, we're going to install the plug-in. So let's go to our WordPress dashboard. Then click on plugins and select add new. In the search bar, type ASC plug-in. Once you find it, click install now. Click activate to enable the plug-in. Now that the ASC plug-in is activated, let's start exploring its features.

## Hiding Admin Notices to Clean Your Dashboard

Firstly, let's see how this plug-in can organize a WordPress dashboard. Usually, our dashboard would look like this with different admin notices, updates, and plug-in messages. With the plug-in, we can hide all the unwanted things and keep our dashboard clean and focused. To do this, go to tools and click on enhancements. Now go to admin interface. Then enable hide admin notices. Once done, click on save changes. Now refresh your WordPress dashboard. And as you can see, the admin notices are no longer showing on the screen.

## Securing Your Site with a Custom Login URL

Now that we have organized our dashboard, next let's see how to make our site even more secure. By default, every WordPress site has the same login URL which ends with WP-admin or WP-login. Hackers can easily find this and track your site. But with the ASC plug-in, we have the option to change the login URL to anything we want so it cannot be identified by others. 

So now let's see how to change our login URL. Go to the login or login section. Now enable the change login URL option. To set your new login URL, click on expand and here enter your new URL. Once done, click save changes. Now let's check if it worked. First let's try accessing the old login URL. Just go to your website and type in WP-admin. As you can see it shows the page is not found. Now enter the new login URL and we can see that the login page loads successfully. And that's how you can change your WordPress login URL.

## Inserting Custom Code Snippets

Next, let's say you're customizing your website and you want to add small code snippets to make visual changes, insert new elements, or for any reason. Normally, you'd have to install extra plugins, edit theme files to add the codes. But in the ASC plug-in, we have a custom code feature that lets you add codes in one single place and easily modify different parts of your site. No extra tools, no complex steps are needed. 

Now, let's see how to add the custom code to your website. To do that, go to custom code in the AC plugin. Enable the insert head, body, and footer code options. Then click expand to open the fields. Now I'll use a custom code from Google Tag Manager for the header part. Google Tag Manager makes it easy to manage and add scripts to a website without editing the actual code. So go to Google Tag Manager and copy this code. Now go back to WordPress and paste the code here. Once that is done, click save changes. And that's it. The code has now been added to your site. See, it was simple, right? So, with the custom code feature, you can easily add custom code snippets to your site and smoothly make changes.

## Limiting Login Attempts

Okay. Next, have you ever worried if someone would break into your WordPress site by guessing your password over and over again? To prevent this, there's an option in the ASC plug-in to limit the login attempts. So, after a few failed attempts, the user gets logged out for a while. So, now let's see how you can limit the login attempts. To do that, go to security and enable limit login attempts. Now, set the number of failed attempts allowed before a lockout. Once done, click save changes. And that's it. Now, if someone tries to enter the wrong password too many times, they'll be temporarily blocked from logging in.

## Customizing the Login Page Logo

All right. Now, you must have noticed that by default, WordPress shows its logo in the login page. But wouldn't it be nice if we have our own site's logo there instead? We can easily do that with the AS plugin. To do that, go to the login section and enable site identity on login page. Once done, click save changes. So to check this, let's go to the login page and refresh it. And that's it. We've replaced the WordPress logo with our site's logo.

## Ensuring Email Delivery with SMTP Setup

Next, let's make sure WordPress emails are delivered properly. You know, sometimes emails from your site like password resets and contact form messages might not reach your inbox. You know, this can happen when emails are flagged by email servers or go to spam. That's why setting up SMTP is very important. It helps ensure that your emails are delivered properly. 

Normally, setting up SMTP can be a bit complicated, but with the AS plug-in, it's easy and super simple. You can guide your SMTP servers in just a few steps so your emails reach your users reliably right where they should. To do that, go to utilities and enable the email delivery option. Then click expand. Here, enter the sender's name and email. To complete the setup, you'll need a few details for your email servers like SMTP, host, port, username, and password. These are the settings that allow your website to connect your email provider and send emails properly. You can easily find them in the email service account. If you already have these details, you can just add them in the fields. If you don't, you can watch this video to set up your SMTP.

## Duplicating Posts and Pages

Okay. Now, let's say you've created a page on your own website and later you want to make a similar one with just a few changes. But instead of building it from scratch, wouldn't it be easier if you could just duplicate the page and make quick edits? With the A plug-in, we can easily duplicate pages without the need to recreate them from scratch. To duplicate a page, go to content management and enable content duplication. Then click expand. And here you'll see two options for where to go after duplicating. I'll choose the list view as it makes it easy to find the duplicated page. 

To check if this works, go to pages, then all pages, and simply click on duplicate under any page. And just like that, the page is successfully duplicated.

## Enabling and Customizing Maintenance Mode

All right. Next, let's check out another feature called maintenance mode. Sometimes you might need to work on your website without visitors seeing the changes. Maintenance mode helps you with that by temporarily hiding your site. It's like putting your site on a pause while you make updates or improvements, letting your visitors know that your site will be back up soon. So, to enable the maintenance mode, let's go back to the A plug-in, go to tools, and click enhancements. Now go to utilities and enable maintenance mode. 

With the ASC plug-in, you can easily add your own message to the maintenance page. Now instead of showing a plain default message, you can write something that looks better and matches your style. So to do that, click expand. And here you can add a custom heading and a description for the maintenance page. Once that is done, click save changes.

## Controlling Image Upload Size

Now, let's open an incognito window and enter a website address. As you can see, we've got the message that we added. 

All right. Next, let's say your site has a lot of images with a large file size. It can really slow down your website and take up a lot of space. In our plug-in, we have an option to set a size limit for images, so your images will adjust to the right size when you upload them, saving you a lot of space and keeping your site at optimal speed. So, let's see how you can do that. Head over to optimizations and turn on image upload control. Click expand. And here you can set the maximum width and the maximum height for uploaded images. Once that is set, click save changes.

## Testing the Image Resizing Feature

Now let's test it out. Go to media and click add new media file. This is the image that we are going to upload. And before uploading let's take the image details. And as you can see the current dimensions are quite high. Now let's drag and drop the image to upload it. Once it is uploaded click edit. And as you can see the image has been resized to match the dimensions we applied and the image still looks just as clear.

## Organizing the Admin Menu

Sometimes the WordPress dashboard can feel crowded with too many menu options. This can make it harder to find what you need and it can slow you down. But no worries, we can customize the admin menu layout and make everything way easier to use. To do that, go to admin interface and enable the admin menu organizer. And here you can rearrange the menu items by simply dragging and dropping them like this. And if you want to rename a menu, just click on it and type a new name. You can also hide some items until toggled by clicking show all at the bottom of the admin menu. Once done, click save changes.

## Redirecting 404 Error Pages

Now, imagine one of your pages isn't working properly. Maybe it's been moved, deleted, or it has an error. When that happens, visitors are usually shown an error page, which is a 404 page. It can happen to anyone, right? But instead of leaving your visitors confused, you can just redirect them to the homepage and keep things running smoothly. To do this, go to utilities and enable the redirect 404 to homepage option and click save changes.

## Exploring ASC Plugin Pro Features

All right, so now we've already covered some really cool features of the AS plug-in, but there are even more awesome ones that come with the pro plan. So let's explore the extra features that it offers. Just head over to the description below and click this link and it'll take you to this page. Now let's click on features. Here you can see we have different features. With custom post types, you can easily manage not just your posts and pages, but also products, portfolios, and reviews. In media categories, you can group files into custom folders and drag and drop them around easily to find what you need. And there are plenty of more features that you can explore below. Now, let's check out the pricing plans. You can pick an annual or a lifetime plan with options for solo users, teams, or agencies. So, you can choose what works best for you and get access to all the features.

## Outro & How to Stay Updated

All right, so that's it guys. We've explored the ASC plug-in and how it can manage our WordPress site so much easier. Website learners is now available on WhatsApp. Whenever we have a new video, it comes on this WhatsApp channel. So to join us on WhatsApp, just scan the QR code and click this link. Now click on this follow button and that's it. You'll now receive the latest updates on WhatsApp. If you guys like this video, hit the like button and don't forget to subscribe to Learners. I'll see you guys in the next video. Until then, take care. Bye-bye.
